prompt.context_jp: 新島 圭介たち一家___、貴恵の母の実家に赴いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新島 圭介たち一家___、貴恵の母の実家に赴いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames the Niijima family as the established topic of this scene-setting sentence.

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-setting line that establishes the Niijima family as the topic the narration will follow. は presents them as the known theme and shifts attention onto what they did.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce them as newly introduced information, which clashes with the narrator's framing. も would wrongly imply 'also, in addition to someone else.'

contrast_examples.en: The family (as topic) went to the hometown.
It was the family (new info) who went to the hometown.

prompt.context_jp: 座敷には料理___並び、久しぶりに顔を合わせた親族の声が幾重にも重なっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 座敷には料理___並び、…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the dishes as new information filling the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is painting the room for the first time — dishes come into view as fresh visual information, which calls for が. The dishes are not a pre-established topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 料理 into a known theme being contrasted or commented on, which doesn't fit this fresh descriptive moment. を is wrong because 並び here is intransitive ('are lined up').

contrast_examples.en: There is a book on the desk (new info).
The book (topic) is on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: 陽射し___廊下の板目に細く落ち、庭では風鈴の音が遠く鳴っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 陽射し___廊下の板目に細く落ち、庭では風鈴の音が遠く鳴っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that pairs 陽射し with the contrasting 庭では later in the sentence.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence lines up two scene elements — the sunlight indoors versus the wind chime outside. は sets up that contrastive parallel between the two clauses.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply report the sunlight as a neutral event and lose the paired contrast with 庭では. を doesn't fit an intransitive verb like 落ちる used this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 姉は本を読み、弟はテレビを見ていた。
contrast_examples.en: The sister read a book, while the brother watched TV.
(It was) the sister who was reading a book.

prompt.context_jp: 言葉と言葉の間に、思いのほか長い間___落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 言葉と言葉の間に、思いのほか長い間___落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that reports the pause as a newly occurring event.

feedback.correct_en: The long silence is a new, noticed event in the narration — が highlights it as fresh information falling between their words.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 間 as an already-known topic, which doesn't match a moment the narrator is just noticing. で would read as a location/means marker and break the sentence.

prompt.context_jp: 蓮司___、伝えるべきことを慎重に選び直しているようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蓮司___、伝えるべきことを慎重に選び直しているようだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that keeps Renji as the known topic the narrator is describing.

feedback.correct_en: Renji has just been named in the preceding call; the narrator now comments on his behavior as the ongoing topic, which is prototypical は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce Renji as new information, undoing the fact that he's already the known speaker in this scene. の would turn him into a modifier of what follows.

prompt.context_jp: 「貴恵___甘やかしすぎたのよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵___甘やかしすぎたのよ
prompt.prompt_en: Aunt is identifying who spoiled Tomori. Choose the particle that pinpoints Takae as THE one who did it.

feedback.correct_en: The aunt is pointing out Takae as the specific person responsible — an exhaustive-listing / identifying use of が ('it was Takae who spoiled him').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would soften this into a general comment about Takae as topic, losing the accusatory 'she's the one' force. を is wrong because 貴恵 is the subject, not the object.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who did it.
As for me, I did it.

prompt.context_jp: 伯母の重い一言のあと、座には短い沈黙___流れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 座には短い沈黙___流れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that reports a new silence settling over the room.

feedback.correct_en: The topic slot is already taken by 座には; the sentence then reports the newly arising silence with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would create a double topic and strip the moment of its 'suddenly-noticed' feel. に would make 沈黙 a target, breaking the grammar.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋には沈黙が流れた。
contrast_examples.en: A silence fell over the room.

prompt.context_jp: 母屋の柱時計の音___、やけに大きく聞こえた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母屋の柱時計の音___、やけに大きく聞こえた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that describes the clock's sound as suddenly standing out.

feedback.correct_en: In this charged silent moment, the clock's ticking is newly salient — が marks that sudden sensory intrusion.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the clock into an established topic being contrasted, losing the 'all at once I noticed' quality. も would wrongly imply 'the clock also, in addition to something else.'

contrast_examples.en: The sound of a clock could be heard (noticed).

prompt.context_jp: 夕方の風___まだ冷たく、田んぼの畔に沿う道は昔と少しも変わっていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕方の風___まだ冷たく、田んぼの畔に沿う道は昔と少しも変わっていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that parallels 風 with the following 道は in a two-part scene description.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence has a 'A は …, B は …' rhythm pairing the wind and the path. は marks each as a theme being commented on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn the wind into breaking news and ruin the parallel with 道は. で reads as a means/place marker and is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: The sea is blue, the sky is vast.

prompt.context_jp: 隣に座る万理華___、急かすでもなく、ただ静かに娘の呼吸を待っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隣に座る万理華___、急かすでもなく、…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that keeps Mariha as the topic whose patient behavior is described.

feedback.correct_en: Mariha is already present in the scene; the narrator comments on how she waits. は sets her up as the known theme for the whole characterization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present her as newly entering the picture, which doesn't match the ongoing scene. を can't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 母は静かに待っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 万理華の言葉___、麻衣の胸のいちばん奥に、まっすぐ届いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 万理華の言葉___、麻衣の胸のいちばん奥に、まっすぐ届いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks Mariha's words as the theme whose impact is being described.

feedback.correct_en: The 'words' were just quoted; now the narrator comments on what they did. は picks them up as the established topic of this reflective sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-announce the words as new information, odd right after they were spoken. で would mark them as a means and doesn't fit 届く.

contrast_examples.jp: その言葉は胸に届いた。
一つの言葉が胸に届いた。

prompt.context_jp: 圭介の言葉のあと、萌子の目にほんの少し光___滲んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 萌子の目にほんの少し光___滲んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that captures the glimmer appearing as a newly observed detail.

feedback.correct_en: A faint light welling up in her eyes is a fresh visual event; が reports it as newly surfacing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the light as a known topic being contrasted, which is strange for something just now appearing. を can't mark the subject of 滲む here.

contrast_examples.en: Tears welled up in her eyes (new event).

prompt.context_jp: 蓮司の姿を見つけた瞬間、頬___熱くなるのを隠しておくことができなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頬___熱くなるのを隠しておくことができなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the embedded clause that reports her cheeks heating up as a sudden sensation.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜のを clause the subject is almost always marked with が, and here the warmth is a fresh bodily event, which fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: は normally doesn't appear inside such embedded noun clauses; it would also wrongly make 頬 a topic. に would mark a destination, not a subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 頬が熱くなるのを感じた。
contrast_examples.en: I felt my cheeks grow hot.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介の言葉に、万理華___少しだけ肩を寄せた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 圭介の言葉に、万理華___少しだけ肩を寄せた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that keeps Mariha as the known subject whose quiet reaction is reported.

feedback.correct_en: Mariha is the ongoing topic of this quiet domestic scene; the sentence just adds another thing she does. は fits this flowing narrative continuity.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as if newly identified, which breaks the warm continuity. を can't mark her as the agent.

contrast_examples.en: It was she who moved first.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣は深く息を吸い、通話ボタン___指を置いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 通話ボタン___指を置いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the call button as the surface her finger comes to rest on.

feedback.correct_en: 置く takes に for the landing point — the finger comes to rest on the button, so the button is marked with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the button as a location of activity, which doesn't fit a stationary 'placing' meaning. を would make the button the direct object, bumping 指 out of its role.

contrast_examples.en: I put the book on the desk.
I read a book at the desk.

prompt.context_jp: 縁側の板の冷たさ___、素足の裏からゆっくり伝わってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 縁側の板の冷たさ___、素足の裏からゆっくり伝わってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that presents the coldness as a newly perceived sensation.

feedback.correct_en: A sensation seeping in from the floor is a fresh perception for Mai; が marks that newly-felt subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the coldness a pre-established topic, which doesn't fit a moment of just-now noticing. を can't mark the subject of 伝わる.

contrast_examples.jp: 冷たさが伝わってきた。
冷たさはずっと残っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 口を開こうとした圭介より先に、彼のほう___決意を告げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼のほう___決意を告げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that identifies HIM — not Keisuke — as the one who spoke first.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts two possible speakers and singles out Tomori as the one who actually spoke — classic identifying が ('X のほうが' = X is the one').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the pointed contrast and read oddly after 〜より先に. も would wrongly suggest 'he too, in addition.'

contrast_examples.jp: 弟のほうが先に話した。
contrast_examples.en: It was the younger brother who spoke first.

prompt.context_jp: ポケットの中で震え続けていた着信を、これ以上___ことはできなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: これ以上___ことはできなかった
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that means 'leave alone / ignore' and fits this reluctant moment with Renji's call.

feedback.correct_en: ほうっておく is the idiomatic verb for 'leave as it is / let go unaddressed,' which fits ignoring a vibrating phone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見逃す means 'overlook / let slip past the eye,' not 'leave untouched over time.' 預かる means 'to keep/hold on behalf of someone,' which is unrelated.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題をほうっておけない。
contrast_examples.en: I can't leave the problem unattended.

contrast_examples.jp: 小さなミスを見逃した。

prompt.context_jp: ___夏を終わらせるわけにはいかない、とだけは思っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___夏を終わらせるわけにはいかない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase that captures 'without clearing up the misunderstanding.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜のまま means 'in that unchanged state,' so 誤解のまま = 'while the misunderstanding still stands.' That's exactly Mai's dilemma here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のうえ means 'on top of' or 'moreover,' which doesn't fit. 〜のたびに means 'every time,' also wrong for a single lingering state.

contrast_examples.en: I slept with my clothes still on.
We talk every time we meet.

prompt.context_jp: 「昔っから ___なとこだけ 頼りになるのよね あなたって人は」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___なとこだけ 頼りになる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective Mariha uses to tease Keisuke — 'you only come through on the ___ parts.'

feedback.correct_en: 肝心 means 'crucial / the parts that really matter.' Mariha is affectionately saying Keisuke steps up exactly when it counts.
feedback.incorrect_en: 派手 ('flashy') doesn't fit — she's praising substance, not showiness. 退屈 ('boring') would make no sense as praise for being reliable.

prompt.context_jp: 強い口調の下に、ずっと畳んでいた疲れが___見えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 疲れが___見えた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that captures fatigue 'showing through' Moeko's tough tone.

feedback.correct_en: 透けて見える is the standard collocation for a hidden feeling becoming visible through a surface — exactly the image here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 溶けて means 'melt,' which doesn't suit emotions becoming visible. 崩れて means 'crumble/collapse,' far too dramatic for this subtle hint of exhaustion.

prompt.context_jp: 「怖いんだよね うっかり期待しちゃって あとで とんでもなく ___のが」
prompt.prompt_jp: とんでもなく ___のが
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits Mai's fear of being 'badly let down' after getting her hopes up.

feedback.correct_en: ヘコむ = 'to feel down/deflated'; the passive-causative ヘコまされる means 'to be made to feel awful' — matches her dread of a crash after hope.
feedback.incorrect_en: 励まされる ('be encouraged') is the opposite of what she fears. 甘やかされる ('be spoiled/pampered') doesn't fit the emotional-letdown context.

contrast_examples.jp: 試験に落ちてヘコんだ。
contrast_examples.en: I was down after failing the exam.
I was encouraged by a friend.

prompt.context_jp: 「本当に___ました また すぐに伺いますんで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 本当に___ました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the set phrase Keisuke uses to thank the aunt for her hospitality.

feedback.correct_en: お世話になりました is the fixed polite expression for thanking someone who hosted or helped you — exactly what Keisuke says on leaving.
feedback.incorrect_en: お疲れになり would be the honorific of 'being tired,' not a thank-you. お手数になり isn't a real set phrase (the real one is お手数をおかけしました).

contrast_examples.jp: お手数をおかけしました。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry for the trouble I caused you.

prompt.context_jp: 白石の口から出かかった説明が、そのまま___を失って喉の奥に沈んでいく。
prompt.prompt_jp: そのまま___を失って喉の奥に沈んでいく
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that completes 'lost its ___' — the explanation has nowhere to go.

feedback.correct_en: 行き場を失う ('lose a place to go') is the idiomatic image for words or feelings that can't find expression — perfect here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 出番を失う ('lose one's turn') is used for roles/opportunities, not for words sinking back. 機嫌を失う isn't an idiom; 機嫌を損ねる is the real phrase.

contrast_examples.en: To lose one's chance to play a part.

prompt.context_jp: ただ、それ以上に、___ものが胸の奥にはっきりと在った。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ものが胸の奥にはっきりと在った
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that describes what Keisuke 'cannot yield / cannot give up' deep in his heart.

feedback.correct_en: 譲る here means 'to concede/compromise'; its potential-negative 譲れない captures something he refuses to give up — his love for his wife.
feedback.incorrect_en: 動けない ('can't move') doesn't fit an inner value. 触れない ('can't touch') describes contact, not refusal to compromise.

contrast_examples.en: This one point I won't yield on.

contrast_examples.jp: それには触れたくない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't want to touch on that topic.

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke is reassuring Mariha about her mother.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Keisuke's gentle reassurance to his wife?

choices.text: お義母さんのことは 僕も一緒に考えるから 心配しないで
お義母さんのことを 僕も一緒に考えるから 心配しないで
お義母さんのこと 僕も一緒に考えてあげるから 心配しないで

feedback.correct_en: The topic-marked 〜のことは opens the sentence smoothly and matches the real line Keisuke speaks. It signals 'about that matter — I'm with you on it.'
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B uses を, which makes the clause too action-focused and awkward with 一緒に考える. Option C's 〜てあげる sounds condescending to one's own wife, breaking the warm equal tone.

contrast_examples.jp: そのことは一緒に考えよう。
そのことを考えてあげる。
contrast_examples.en: I'll think about that for you (sounds patronizing).

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke declines Moriya's feelings carefully.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally declines someone's feelings in a sincere, polite way?

choices.text: 守屋さんの気持ちには 応えられません
守屋さんの気持ちを 応えられません
守屋さんの気持ちで 応えられません

feedback.correct_en: 応える takes に for the thing you respond to (気持ちに応える = 'reciprocate feelings'). That's the collocation Keisuke actually uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is ungrammatical with 応える in this sense. で would mark feelings as a means, which makes no sense here.

prompt.context_jp: Mariha speaks hopefully about the future with Keisuke by the kotatsu.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'let's keep updating our happiness'?

choices.text: もっともっと 新しい幸せを 更新していきましょ
もっともっと 新しい幸せが 更新していきましょ
もっともっと 新しい幸せに 更新していきましょ

feedback.correct_en: 更新する takes を for the thing being updated/renewed. 幸せを更新する ('keep renewing happiness') is the natural pairing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 幸せ the subject that updates itself, which doesn't work with the volitional 〜ましょ. に would mark a goal, breaking the collocation.

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke insists Tomori has his sister's kindness inside him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'Takae's kindness is also surely inside Tomori'?

choices.text: 貴恵が持っていた優しさが 確かに 友利くんの中にもある
貴恵は持っていた優しさは 確かに 友利くんの中にもある
貴恵が持っていた優しさは 確かに 友利くんの中にもあった

feedback.correct_en: Inside the relative clause 貴恵が持っていた, が marks the subject naturally; the outer sentence then uses が again to present the kindness as the key thing that exists in Tomori.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B replaces the relative-clause が with は, which is ungrammatical inside a modifier. Option C's past tense あった wrongly implies the kindness is no longer present.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が書いた本を読んだ。
contrast_examples.en: I read the book that he wrote (relative clause takes が).

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は書いた本を読んだ。
contrast_examples.en: He (topic) read the book he wrote (different meaning).

prompt.context_jp: Mai comforts Renji about his lost childhood friend.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'the feeling of wishing for a miracle, I understand'?

choices.text: 奇跡を願う気持ち 分かるから
奇跡が願う気持ち 分かるから
奇跡に願う気持ち 分かるから

feedback.correct_en: 願う takes を for what is wished for. 奇跡を願う ('to wish for a miracle') is the standard collocation Mai uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 奇跡 the thing doing the wishing, which is nonsense. に is used with 願う only for the person being asked (神に願う), not the content of the wish.
